title: Short Stuff: Firewalking
summary: Short Stuff episode on firewalking. The hosts note the practice dates back at least 3,200 years to an ancient Indian text and has spread worldwide (India, Greece, China, Spain, Japan, Bulgaria, Thailand, Tibet, Fiji), usually as a religious or commemorative rite. They cover the 1930s experiments by the University of London Council for Psychical Research (1935 and 1937) that showed firewalking was not special or spiritual, the New Age revival in the 1970s and 80s with metaphysical explanations, and the physics: embers rather than flames, wood choice (cherry or maple), the insulating ash layer, and brief foot contact at a brisk pace. They mention a 2012 Tony Robbins firewalk event where 21 people were treated for burns, and close with a strong warning not to try it.

segments.title: Introduction and history of firewalking
segments.summary: The hosts introduce firewalking and discuss its history, saying it dates back at least 3,200 years to an ancient Indian text and has spread worldwide, usually as a religious or commemorative practice.

segments.title: 1930s experiments debunk firewalking
segments.summary: The University of London Council for Psychical Research ran experiments in 1935 and 1937 with British scientists and people from native cultures, showing firewalking was not religious or special. The New Age movement later adopted it with metaphysical explanations, which renewed interest in debunking.
topics: University of London Council for Psychical Research

segments.title: Physics of firewalking
segments.summary: The hosts explain the physics: walkers cross hot embers rather than flames, specific woods such as cherry or maple make bright but poorly conducting coals, a layer of ash insulates the feet, and contact time is under half a second at a brisk pace.

segments.title: Firewalking injuries and Tony Robbins event
segments.summary: The hosts note firewalks can go wrong, citing a 2012 Tony Robbins event where 21 people were treated for burns, and discuss Robbins's hands-on style.

segments.title: Warnings and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts joke about trying firewalking, strongly warn listeners not to attempt it, and sign off with a closing credit.
